docs.text: Driver BMP581 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Bosch BMP581 barometric pressure and temperature sensor, on I2C or SPI. It starts the chip from a soft reset, measures on request or continuously, reads the FIFO, and never returns a stuck line, a reset value or an out-of-range reading as a measurement, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: the soft reset and the post-power-up checks, the configuration written in standby and read back, the power modes, the data and FIFO reads, the conversion to pascals and degrees Celsius, and the reset check. Barometric pressure sensor BMP581 Bosch Sensortec Function Absolute pressure, 30 kPa to 125 kPa at 1/64 Pa per count; temperature, -40 °C to 85 °C at 1/65536 °C; compensated on the chip Interface I2C up to 1 MHz at 0x46 or 0x47 (SDO), or four-wire SPI up to 12 MHz, mode 0 or 3; I3C (not used here) Modes Standby and deep standby; forced (one measurement); normal at 0.125 Hz to 240 Hz; continuous Data Oversampling x1 to x128, an IIR filter, a 32-frame FIFO, interrupts for data ready, FIFO full and threshold, and pressure out of range Supply VDD 1.71 V to 3.6 V, VDDIO 1.08 V to 3.6 V; 1.3 µA at 1 Hz in low-power mode What you get ¶ One object per chip, on either bus. BMP581<YourPort> takes a reference to an I2C or an SPI port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Values you can trust. One 12-byte read per measurement, checked for stuck and floating lines, the reset value and the measurement range before a value is returned; FIFO frames carry their own validity. See Contract . Resets found, never written over. A brown-out mid-session is found by the next read or setter, confirmed by a second read, and reported as DeviceReset ; nothing cached is written over the reset chip. See Contract . Datasheet defaults. Config{} holds the chip's reset values with units in the field names, plus four presets; Validate() checks the ranges and the data rate table. See Configuration . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus hooks and a delay, plus optional failure and logging hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests and a fuzzer run the driver against a register model of the chip that measures, resets and fails on its own. See Testing and CI . API guide ¶ Common tasks with bmp581::BMP581<Port> , task by task. Every call returns Result<T> ; check it before using the value. The API reference lists every member. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Bosch Sensortec BST-BMP581-DS004-13 1.13: Measurement range, resolution and accuracy: 2 Specification; Table 1 Pressure Performance; Table 2 Temperature Performance, p. 8 Power modes, deep standby and mode transitions: 4.3 Power modes; 4.3.1 STANDBY mode; 4.3.2 DEEP STANDBY; 4.3.7 Mode transitions, p. 16 Forced mode: 4.3.3 FORCED mode, p. 16 Data registers and data shadowing: 4.5 Data registers; 4.5.1 Data Shadowing, p. 22 FIFO: 4.6 FIFO; 4.6.1 FIFO Configuration; 4.6.3 FIFO data readout; Tables 11 to 14, p. 22 FIFO flush on configuration changes: 4.6.4 FIFO configuration changes; Table 4 t_reconf, p. 25 Interrupt sources, out of range and power-on reset: 4.7 Interrupts; 4.7.2.3 Out-of-range interrupt; 4.7.2.4 Power-on reset interrupt, p. 25 Register map: 7 Register Map, p. 50 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Start the chip ¶ bmp581 :: Error BringUp ( Sensor & sensor ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call; later calls run the reset check and // start again when the chip reset. After a failure the next call starts from the beginning. const auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "BMP581 init: %s 
 " , bmp581 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } The first call soft-resets the chip and configures it (about 5 ms); a later call checks for a reset with one 3-byte read. Nothing touches the chip before it: every other call returns NotInitialized . Measure on request (forced mode) ¶ bmp581 :: Result < bmp581 :: Measurement > SampleOnDemand ( Sensor & sensor ) { // Standby between calls (deep standby with Config{}); one forced measurement per call. return sensor . MeasureOnce (); // reset check, forced, poll until standby, one 12-byte read } The configured mode stays standby (deep standby with Config{} ), and each MeasureOnce() runs one measurement: the reset check, ODR_CONFIG = forced, a read that proves it started, a wait of the typical conversion time less 5 %, polls until the chip is back in standby (at most ForcedMeasurementMaxUs() , Timeout after), and the data read. In normal or continuous mode it returns Busy with nothing sent. Measurement holds the chip's own units. Convert with PressurePa(m.pressure_raw) (1/64 Pa per count) and TemperatureC(m.temperature_raw) (1/65536 °C per count); both are exact. Stream in normal mode ¶ bmp581 :: Error StreamAt25Hz ( Sensor & sensor , int samples ) { // HighResolutionPreset(): normal mode, 25 Hz, x16 pressure, IIR, data-ready source on. if ( auto r = sensor . ApplyConfig ( bmp581 :: HighResolutionPreset ()); ! r ) { return r . error ; } for ( int i = 0 ; i < samples ; ++ i ) { if ( auto r = sensor . WaitDataReady (); ! r ) { return r . error ; // Timeout, or DeviceReset: call EnsureInitialized() } const auto m = sensor . ReadMeasurement (); if ( ! m ) { return m . error ; } std :: printf ( "%.3f Pa 
 " , static_cast < double > ( bmp581 :: PressurePa ( m . value . pressure_raw ))); } return bmp581 :: Error :: Ok ; } WaitDataReady() polls INT_STATUS every kPollUs until drdy, at most Config::data_ready_timeout_ms ; it needs Config::source_data_ready (the chip reports drdy only for an enabled source, section 4.7.1). ReadMeasurement() reads the data registers whatever the mode; in standby it returns the last measurement. Each INT_STATUS read clears the flags on the chip; the driver keeps them in a latch, GetLatchedInterrupts() , until ClearLatchedInterrupts() . SetPowerMode() changes the mode alone: standby, normal or continuous, always through standby and read back. In normal mode the chip checks the data rate against the oversampling; when it disagrees (OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid = 0) the call returns ConfigRejected and leaves the chip in standby. Validate() refuses those combinations first, from table 7. Read the FIFO ¶ std :: size_t DrainFifo ( Sensor & sensor , std :: span < bmp581 :: FifoSample > out ) { // FifoPreset(): pressure-and-temperature frames at 10 Hz, threshold at 8 frames. const auto n = sensor . ReadFifo ( out ); if ( ! n ) { return 0 ; // InvalidReply (a stuck line) or DeviceReset } std :: size_t good = 0 ; for ( std :: size_t i = 0 ; i < n . value ; ++ i ) { good += ( out [ i ]. error == bmp581 :: Error :: Ok ) ? 1U : 0U ; // each frame has its own validity } return good ; } ReadFifo() reads FIFO_COUNT, then whole frames in one burst from FIFO_DATA, as many as out holds; the rest stay. Each FifoSample has its own error : NoData for the empty frame (0x7F7F7F), OutOfRange . A temperature-and-pressure frame fills both values; a single-value frame says which one it has. A configuration change flushes the FIFO (section 4.6.4). An empty FIFO runs the reset check, because a reset empties it. Handle a reset ¶ bmp581 :: Error Supervise ( Sensor & sensor ) { // A brown-out resets the chip to standby with every register at its reset value. Every data // read checks for it; CheckForReset() does it alone (one 2-byte read). const auto r = sensor . CheckForReset (); if ( r . error == bmp581 :: Error :: DeviceReset ) { return sensor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // soft reset and the configuration, again } return r . error ; } Data reads, polls and setters find a reset by themselves and return DeviceReset ; the driver is then uninitialised, so the next call is EnsureInitialized() . How the driver tells a reset from a broken line: Contract . Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( bmp581 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case bmp581 :: Error :: NoDevice : case bmp581 :: Error :: Bus : case bmp581 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check the wiring, CSB and SDO, and the address" ; case bmp581 :: Error :: InvalidReply : return "a line is stuck or floating: check pull-ups and SDO" ; case bmp581 :: Error :: DeviceReset : return "the chip reset: call EnsureInitialized()" ; case bmp581 :: Error :: OutOfRange : return "outside 30 to 125 kPa or -40 to 85 degrees C" ; default : return bmp581 :: ToString ( e ); } } Error What to do NoDevice , Bus Check power, wiring and the address (I2C) or CSB (SPI); retry EnsureInitialized() DeviceIdMismatch Another part answers, or the soft reset did not happen: see Troubleshooting InvalidReply A line is stuck, floating or disturbed: check pull-ups, SDO, CSB; the next call reads again DeviceReset Call EnsureInitialized() NoData No measurement since the reset: start one ( MeasureOnce() , normal mode) OutOfRange The environment is outside the sensor's range, or the reading is wrong WriteMismatch , StateUnknown Call ApplyConfig() again; check the bus Timeout See Troubleshooting Busy Switch to standby before MeasureOnce() Unsupported Enable the data-ready source or the FIFO in Config ConfigRejected Lower the data rate or the oversampling (table 7) Crc is never returned: neither bus carries a CRC. Diagnostics and raw access ¶ ReadRegister(address) reads one register once, with no retry (KB-CPP-129); FIFO_DATA and CMD are refused. A raw INT_STATUS read clears the flags and feeds the latch. GetLastIntStatus() , GetLastStatus() , GetLastOsrEff() , GetRevision() return what the last read saw, with no I/O. ReadInterruptStatus() reads INT_STATUS once and decodes it. ReadMeasurement(Verify::ReadBack) and ReadFifo(out, Verify::ReadBack) add the reset check, one 3-byte read. ReadMeasurement(Verify::ReadBack) and MeasureOnce(Verify::ReadBack) also read the data registers a second time (6 bytes, a third when they differ): a bit flipped inside a data byte is not detectable without it. Shut down ¶ void PowerDown ( Sensor & sensor ) { // One byte, CMD = 0xB6: deep standby with the reset values, proved by INT_STATUS.por. if ( auto r = sensor . Deinitialize (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "BMP581 soft reset not proved: %s 
 " , bmp581 :: ToString ( r . error )); } } Deinitialize() always does its work, also before a start or after a reset; the driver is uninitialised afterwards either way.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens in each when you take a measurement. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Bosch Sensortec BST-BMP581-DS004-13 1.13: Supplies, timing and conversion times: 2 Specification; Table 4 Electrical characteristics, p. 10 Register writes only in standby: 4.3.8 Mode-depending register write restrictions, p. 18 Post-power-up checks: 4.3.9 Post-power-up procedure, p. 18 Soft reset: 4.3.10 Soft reset; 7.36 Register (0x7E) Command Register, p. 18 Data registers and data shadowing: 4.5 Data registers; 4.5.1 Data Shadowing, p. 22 Read burst address increment: 5.4 Read burst address increment, p. 36 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/bmp581.hpp public calls ; inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/bmp581.hpp , src/bmp581.ipp Lifecycle, configuration, power modes, measurements, the FIFO, the reset check, errors Types and registers inc/bmp581_types.hpp , inc/bmp581_registers.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config and presets, timing and range constants, the conversions; the register map Port contracts inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp , inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp Each bus's CRTP base, its concept ( I2cPort , SpiPort ), its bus requirements and its register framing Platform port Your class Bus bring-up and byte transfers, delays, optionally the failure reason (I2C) and logging Kconfig layer inc/bmp581_kconfig.hpp Optional: a Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig Two buses, one driver ¶ The register model is the same on both buses; only the framing differs (sections 5.5, 5.6): I2C SPI Read WriteRead() : the address, then the data One frame: address with bit 7 set, then the data Write Write() : address and one data byte One frame: address with bit 7 clear, one data byte Start-up Nothing extra A dummy read selects SPI, again after each soft reset (section 5.1) Soft reset NACKed by the chip, expected (section 7.36) A normal frame Address NACK NoDevice with GetLastFailure() No ACK on SPI: an absent chip reads as a stuck line BMP581<Port> takes either: the BusPort concept accepts a class that is exactly one of I2cPort and SpiPort , and detail::BusFor<Port> picks I2cRegisterBus or SpiRegisterBus at compile time. Both framings expose the same four operations (select the interface, read a burst, write one register, write the reset command), so the core has no bus-specific code. Every write is one register in one transfer: the chip stores it whole or not at all, and SPI would need an address per byte in a burst anyway (figure 9). One measurement through the layers ¶ From a conversion to a value Figure description and sources Two entry points at the top. MeasureOnce() runs the reset check (INT_STATUS, then OSR_CONFIG to OSR_EFF in one read), writes ODR_CONFIG with pwr_mode = forced, polls it until it shows forced (at most t_startup) to prove the measurement started, waits the typical conversion time less 5 percent, then polls the same registers until the chip is back in standby, at most the datasheet maximum. In normal or continuous mode, WaitDataReady() polls INT_STATUS until drdy. Both end in the same read: one 12-byte burst of TEMP_DATA to STATUS, so temperature and pressure come from one conversion (data shadowing). The checks below run in order, and each failure has its error card on the right: the reserved registers must read 0x00 and the frame must not be all 0x00 (a stuck or floating line); INT_STATUS goes to the latch, and a por in it runs the reset check; the reset value 0x7F7F7F is no measurement and runs the reset check too; the values must lie in the measurement range. Only then is the value returned, in 1/64 Pa and 1/65536 degrees Celsius. Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by a concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Optional hooks by named concepts. DelayUs , GetLastFailure and Log are detected by Declares* and Has* concepts in bmp581::detail . One read buffer, owned by the driver. A value is copied out of the buffer before any later read (the reset check) reuses it. No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . docs.text: The register model is the same on both buses; only the framing differs (sections 5.5, 5.6): I2C SPI Read WriteRead() : the address, then the data One frame: address with bit 7 set, then the data Write Write() : address and one data byte One frame: address with bit 7 clear, one data byte Start-up Nothing extra A dummy read selects SPI, again after each soft reset (section 5.1) Soft reset NACKed by the chip, expected (section 7.36) A normal frame Address NACK NoDevice with GetLastFailure() No ACK on SPI: an absent chip reads as a stuck line BMP581<Port> takes either: the BusPort concept accepts a class that is exactly one of I2cPort and SpiPort , and detail::BusFor<Port> picks I2cRegisterBus or SpiRegisterBus at compile time. Both framings expose the same four operations (select the interface, read a burst, write one register, write the reset command), so the core has no bus-specific code. Every write is one register in one transfer: the chip stores it whole or not at all, and SPI would need an address per byte in a burst anyway (figure 9).

[Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The repository moved to kokeb-labs-drivers; URLs follow. [0.1.0] - 2026-11-10 ¶ Added ¶ Driver. bmp581::BMP581<Port> for the Bosch BMP581 (datasheet BST-BMP581-DS004-13, revision 1.13), on I2C ( I2cInterface , I2cPort ) or four-wire SPI ( SpiInterface , SpiPort ), the bus chosen by the port type ( BusPort ). Start-up. EnsureInitialized() : power-up wait, the SPI selection read, a soft reset, CHIP_ID, NVM ready and INT_STATUS = 0x10 then 0x00 (section 4.3.9), then standby with deep standby off (the reset leaves the chip in deep standby, where writes need not land, section 4.3), the reset marker in NVM_DATA, and the configuration one register per transfer, ODR_CONFIG last, read back in full. Deinitialize() : a soft reset into deep standby, proved by INT_STATUS. Every soft reset is preceded by standby with deep standby off. Measurements. MeasureOnce() (forced mode, polled until it shows as started, at most t_startup, then polled to standby within the datasheet maximum), SetPowerMode() (standby, normal, continuous, through standby, read back; in normal mode OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid polled too, ConfigRejected only at the deadline; with the FIFO on, t_reconf for the FIFO flush before Ok ), WaitDataReady() , ReadMeasurement() (one 12-byte read of TEMP_DATA to STATUS); PressurePa() , TemperatureC() and SignExtend24() , exact. FIFO and interrupts. ReadFifo() with a validity per frame, ReadFifoCount() , ReadInterruptStatus() , the latch ( GetLatchedInterrupts() ), the INT pin, the four sources and the out-of-range window in Config . Values. No frame of a stuck or floating line (reserved registers, reserved bits, all 0x00, all 0xFF), no reset value 0x7F7F7F and nothing outside 30 kPa to 125 kPa or -40 °C to 85 °C is returned as a value. Verify::ReadBack on ReadMeasurement() and MeasureOnce() reads the data again, so a bit flipped inside a data byte is outvoted or refused. Resets. OSR_CONFIG.press_en (always written 1) is the reset sentinel, read with ODR_CONFIG and OSR_EFF and their reserved bits, so no constant byte passes; a marker in NVM_DATA, verified or written in standby before every configuration sequence and counted only until the next measurement from deep standby (whose NVM download may overwrite it, 0x00 0x00 included), shows a reset that a sequence's own writes covered; INT_STATUS.por, the reset value of the data registers, an empty FIFO and an empty or out-of-range FIFO frame run the reset check; on SPI every status, FIFO and raw read runs it before returning (the frame that only selects SPI, section 5.1); evidence is confirmed by a second read; setters read INT_STATUS and the sentinel before they write; a por the sentinel contradicts is decided by the whole configuration and the marker; a check that cannot be read stays pending ( DeviceReset , CheckForReset() ). Doubt. A failed standby or mode write leaves the configuration in doubt ( IsConfigKnown() , StateUnknown ); a configuration sequence that fails after its first write leaves the driver uninitialised; standby and Deinitialize() are never refused, also after a failed first start that reached the chip. Configuration. Config with the datasheet reset values, Validate() with table 7 and the INT pad drive rule of section 7.5 (8 and up with open drain only), CheckedConfig , the presets ForcedPreset() , LowPowerPreset() , HighResolutionPreset() , FifoPreset() , and KconfigDefaults() . Tests and docs. Host tests over a register model that measures and resets on its own and offers each open reading of the datasheet as a knob (deep standby losing writes, odr_is_valid and mode lags, the SPI selection fill), a fuzz target with the safety rules as invariants and no skips, chip diagrams (pinout, blocks, the I2C and SPI connections, a MISO pull-up on SPI), the start-up and measurement figures, and the host and ESP32 examples.

The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration and the I2C address ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, waits t_powup, soft-resets the chip, checks CHIP_ID, NVM readiness and the reset flag, and only then writes the configuration, in standby, and reads it back. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning. Once started, a later call runs the reset check and returns Ok , or starts again when the chip reset. Every call that touches the chip returns NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, except Deinitialize() . No call starts the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration. InvalidArgument means nothing was sent. Every port failure propagates ( Bus , or NoDevice for an I2C address NACK the port reports); a failed value is T{} . Every wait is bounded by a datasheet maximum or a validated Config timeout: kTimeoutMaxMs at most. Config{} equals the datasheet reset values, except that pressure is always measured ( OSR_CONFIG.press_en ). Values ¶ A measurement comes from one 12-byte read of TEMP_DATA to STATUS, so temperature and pressure come from one conversion (section 4.5.1). No reply a broken line can produce is ever a value: a frame whose reserved registers (0x23 to 0x26) are not 0x00 or whose reserved bits are set (all 0xFF), or a frame of all 0x00, is InvalidReply . The reset value 0x7F7F7F is NoData , never a reading; a value outside 30 kPa to 125 kPa or -40 °C to 85 °C is OutOfRange , never clamped. A FIFO read reports validity per frame ( FifoSample::error ); a FIFO burst of all 0x00 or all 0xFF is InvalidReply for the whole call. The conversions are exact: pressure_raw / 64 Pa and temperature_raw / 65536 °C (section 4.5). Resets ¶ A power-on reset (a supply dip, a brown-out) or a soft reset loads every register with its reset value and sets INT_STATUS.por (sections 4.7.2.4, 7.21). The chip then sits in deep standby (section 4.3): it measures nothing, and a driver that did not notice would keep reading the old data or write its cached settings over the reset chip. The sentinel. The driver always writes OSR_CONFIG with press_en = 1, and only a reset clears it, so OSR_CONFIG.press_en = 0 is the reset. No write of the driver erases it. The marker. 0x3C and 0xC3 in NVM_DATA_LSB and NVM_DATA_MSB (reset value 0x00, inert without an NVM command in CMD, sections 4.8.1, 7.25, 7.26). NVM_DATA is the NVM read port, and the NVM is downloaded at the start of every measurement from deep standby (sections 4.8.1.1, 7.22); the datasheet does not say whether that reaches NVM_DATA, so a download may leave any value there, 0x00 0x00 (an unprogrammed word) included. The driver therefore counts the marker only while it is fresh: written or verified in standby, with no measurement from deep standby since. Every configuration sequence, after the call's reset check and with the chip in standby with deep standby off (no download can follow until the sequence ends), reads NVM_DATA. A fresh marker that reads 0x00 0x00 twice is a reset ( DeviceReset , nothing written). Otherwise anything but the marker is overwritten at once, and the sentinel is read again: the sequence has not written OSR_CONFIG yet, so a reset between the call's check and the new marker still shows. The sequence itself does not write NVM_DATA, so 0x00 0x00 at its read-back is a reset during it, even when the sequence's own OSR_CONFIG write covered the sentinel. The decision on a por the sentinel contradicts uses the marker only while it is fresh; otherwise the configuration alone decides. Any value other than the marker or 0x00 0x00 is the marker lost, never a reset. The evidence. Every INT_STATUS read (data reads, polls, ReadInterruptStatus() , a raw read) is checked for por; the data registers at their reset value are evidence too. Each runs the reset check: OSR_CONFIG, ODR_CONFIG and OSR_EFF in one read. Confirmed before acting. Reset evidence is read a second time: press_en = 0, a reserved bit set in OSR_CONFIG or OSR_EFF (a reply that cannot come from the chip; no constant byte passes these checks, so neither a stuck line nor the SPI frame that only selects SPI again does), or, with the configuration known, OSR_CONFIG or ODR_CONFIG differing from what the driver wrote and read back. A second read that shows it again is the reset: the driver is then uninitialised and returns DeviceReset ; call EnsureInitialized() . One corrupt read costs one more read. Never written over. ApplyConfig() , SetPowerMode() to a measuring mode and MeasureOnce() read INT_STATUS and then OSR_CONFIG and ODR_CONFIG before their first write, and a reset found sends nothing. A por the sentinel contradicts. When INT_STATUS shows por but OSR_CONFIG does not, either the por read was corrupt or a reset was followed by an OSR_CONFIG write (a sequence whose reads were disturbed). With the configuration known, the whole configuration and the marker decide: a chip that no longer holds them reset; one that holds them gives InvalidReply , and the next call checks again. When those reads fail, the decision moves to the next call, which writes nothing before it. Doubt is never dropped. A check that is due but cannot be read stays pending, and no call returns Ok until it has passed: a call that would succeed fails with the check's error, a call that failed keeps its own (a confirmed reset outranks it). In a configuration sequence the sequence itself rewrites OSR_CONFIG, so a por read at its end cannot be confirmed: it is taken as the reset, the safe direction for a sensor. A sequence that fails after its first configuration write leaves the driver uninitialised, whatever the error: a reset during it could hide behind its own writes and a lost INT_STATUS read, so the next EnsureInitialized() starts again from the soft reset. An empty FIFO (with the FIFO on), an empty FIFO frame and a FIFO frame out of range run the reset check too: a reset empties and disables the FIFO. On SPI the first frame after a reset only selects SPI again, and its bytes are whatever MISO shows (section 5.1): an INT_STATUS, FIFO_COUNT, FIFO_DATA or raw read cannot tell such a frame from data. On SPI, ReadInterruptStatus() , WaitDataReady() (when it sees drdy), ReadFifoCount() , ReadFifo() and ReadRegister() therefore run the reset check before they return what they read: one more 3-byte read. The data read needs none: its reserved registers refuse every constant frame. A pull-up on MISO (see Hardware ) makes the frame read 0xFF. A line stuck low reads OSR_CONFIG = 0x00 twice and is reported as a reset; EnsureInitialized() then fails with DeviceIdMismatch . On I2C, calls that only read status ( ReadInterruptStatus() , ReadFifoCount() , ReadRegister() ) report what they read and run the reset check only on evidence; where a supply dip is possible and the application only reads status, call CheckForReset() . A bit flipped inside a data byte. The bus carries no CRC: a single bit flipped by noise inside a data byte (a temperature LSB, a FIFO sample) gives a plausible value that no reserved bit or range check can refuse, and it is not detectable without a second read. ReadMeasurement(Verify::ReadBack) and MeasureOnce(Verify::ReadBack) read TEMP_DATA and PRESS_DATA again (6 bytes): equal is Ok ; otherwise a third read decides, equal to either earlier read (a new measurement in normal or continuous mode, or one disturbed read), and three different values, or two reads of a stuck line, are InvalidReply . A FIFO read cannot be repeated: the frames leave the FIFO. Writes ¶ Every write is one register in one transfer, stored whole or not at all; the driver never writes a burst. The configuration is written in standby with deep standby off, the only state that takes every write (sections 4.3.1, 4.3.8): ODR_CONFIG = standby with deep_dis = 1 and t_standby first, whenever the chip may be measuring or in deep standby, and ODR_CONFIG with the configured deep_dis last. It is read back in full; a power mode change goes through standby (section 4.3.7) and is read back. A forced measurement is polled until pwr_mode shows forced, at most t_startup (3 ms), before the driver waits for it, so a dropped write never returns the old data as new. A write that failed may have landed. A failed standby or mode write leaves the configuration in doubt ( IsConfigKnown() false), and the calls that depend on it ( MeasureOnce() , WaitDataReady() , the FIFO calls, SetPowerMode() to a measuring mode) return StateUnknown with nothing sent until ApplyConfig() or EnsureInitialized() succeeds; a running EnsureInitialized() with the configuration in doubt starts again from the soft reset. A failed or mismatching configuration sequence leaves the driver uninitialised (see Resets ). A mode change is read back until it shows, at most t_startup_deep (4 ms), and in normal mode until OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid = 1 too: the datasheet gives no time for either. ConfigRejected only at the deadline. With the FIFO on, ApplyConfig() and SetPowerMode() return after t_reconf (3 ms): the change flushed the FIFO, and FIFO_COUNT is not to be read before the flush completes (section 4.6.4). SetPowerMode(PowerMode::Standby) and Deinitialize() are never refused once the driver has started: not after a reset was found, not with the configuration in doubt, not with a check pending. Deinitialize() writes ODR_CONFIG = standby with deep_dis = 1 and CMD = 0xB6, and is Ok only when INT_STATUS shows the reset. Every soft reset, at start-up and in Deinitialize() , is preceded by ODR_CONFIG = standby with deep_dis = 1 and t_standby: the datasheet does not say that deep standby takes CMD (section 4.3.1 says standby takes every write). Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates bmp581_version.h Your port The bus within its requirements, CSB idle high on SPI; the delay; optional hooks ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ bmp581::Error inside bmp581::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; this driver returns every one of them except Crc (the bus carries no CRC), plus eight chip-specific values. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran or a reset was found since InvalidArgument 2 A Config field, the address or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 NVM never ready, a forced measurement not ended, standby not reached, or no data ready in time DeviceIdMismatch 5 CHIP_ID is not 0x50, or INT_STATUS did not show the soft reset (0x10, then 0x00) Crc 6 Not returned Busy 7 MeasureOnce() while the chip measures; nothing was sent DeviceFault 8 STATUS reports an NVM error at start-up Unsupported 9 WaitDataReady() without the data-ready source or in standby; a FIFO call with the FIFO off DeviceReset 16 The chip reset, confirmed by a second read; the driver is uninitialised InvalidReply 17 A reply the chip cannot send: a stuck, floating or disturbed line NoDevice 18 An I2C address NACK, with GetLastFailure() NoData 19 The data registers hold their reset value: no measurement since the reset OutOfRange 20 A value outside the measurement range WriteMismatch 21 A register read back differently from what was just written StateUnknown 22 The configuration is in doubt after a failed write; nothing was sent ConfigRejected 23 Normal mode: OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid still 0 at the deadline; the chip was put back in standby The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config , a 96-byte read buffer and a few flags; an SPI driver also holds two 97-byte frame buffers in its framing. The largest stack buffer is 12 bytes (a copy of the data frame). Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

Every soft reset, at start-up and in Deinitialize() , is preceded by ODR_CONFIG = standby with deep_dis = 1 and t_standby: the datasheet does not say that deep standby takes CMD (section 4.3.1 says standby takes every write).

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state.

docs.text: bmp581::Error inside bmp581::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; this driver returns every one of them except Crc (the bus carries no CRC), plus eight chip-specific values. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran or a reset was found since InvalidArgument 2 A Config field, the address or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 NVM never ready, a forced measurement not ended, standby not reached, or no data ready in time DeviceIdMismatch 5 CHIP_ID is not 0x50, or INT_STATUS did not show the soft reset (0x10, then 0x00) Crc 6 Not returned Busy 7 MeasureOnce() while the chip measures; nothing was sent DeviceFault 8 STATUS reports an NVM error at start-up Unsupported 9 WaitDataReady() without the data-ready source or in standby; a FIFO call with the FIFO off DeviceReset 16 The chip reset, confirmed by a second read; the driver is uninitialised InvalidReply 17 A reply the chip cannot send: a stuck, floating or disturbed line NoDevice 18 An I2C address NACK, with GetLastFailure() NoData 19 The data registers hold their reset value: no measurement since the reset OutOfRange 20 A value outside the measurement range WriteMismatch 21 A register read back differently from what was just written StateUnknown 22 The configuration is in doubt after a failed write; nothing was sent ConfigRejected 23 Normal mode: OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid still 0 at the deadline; the chip was put back in standby The API guide says what to do about each.

docs.text: No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config , a 96-byte read buffer and a few flags; an SPI driver also holds two 97-byte frame buffers in its framing. The largest stack buffer is 12 bytes (a copy of the data frame).

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The BMP581's package, pins, connections, bus settings, timing and power, as the driver relies on them. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Bosch Sensortec BST-BMP581-DS004-13 1.13: Measurement range, resolution and accuracy: 2 Specification; Table 1 Pressure Performance; Table 2 Temperature Performance, p. 8 Supplies, timing and conversion times: 2 Specification; Table 4 Electrical characteristics, p. 10 Block diagram and power management: 4.1 Block diagram; 4.2 Power management, p. 14 INT pin: 4.7.3 Interrupt pin, p. 27 Interface selection (I2C, SPI): 5.1 Protocol Selection; Table 16, p. 31 I2C protocol and addresses: 5.6 I2C protocol; 5.6.1 I2C write operation; 5.6.2 I2C read operation, p. 38 Pins and connection diagrams: 6.1 Pin Out; 6.2 Connection Diagrams; Table 28, p. 46 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Package ¶ A 10-pin metal-lid LGA, 2.0 mm x 2.0 mm, at most 0.8 mm high (table 3). The vent hole is on the lid; keep it open, and keep vias, traces and solder mask out from under the part (section 8.2). Pins ¶ Top view of figure 23. There is no reset or enable pin: CSB at power-up selects the interface, and the driver resets the chip with a command. BMP581 pinout, LGA-10 Figure description and sources The BMP581 seen from the top, in its LGA-10 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp ; inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp . LGA-10, 10 pins (6.1 Pin Out, Figure 23, p. 46 ). Pin Name Type (domain) Function Driver hook If unused Datasheet 1 VDDIO power (VDDIO) Digital interface supply, 1.08 V to 3.6 V; any order with VDD - - 2, p. 10 2 SCK bus (VDDIO) Serial clock: I2C SCL, or SPI SCK WriteRead() or Transfer() - 6.1, p. 46 3 VSS ground Ground - - 6.1, p. 46 4 SDI bus (VDDIO) Serial data: I2C SDA, or SPI MOSI (SDX); data in and out in 3-wire SPI WriteRead() or Transfer() - 6.1, p. 46 5 SDO digital in/out (VDDIO) SPI MISO; on I2C the address LSB: VSS 0x46, VDDIO 0x47 Transfer() I2C: tie to VSS or VDDIO, never open 5.6, p. 38 6 CSB digital in (VDDIO) SPI chip select, active low; held at VDDIO from power-up selects I2C Transfer() I2C: tie to VDDIO 5.1, p. 31 7 INT digital out (VDDIO) Interrupt output, push-pull or open drain, polarity set by INT_CONFIG - Tie to GND with INT_CONFIG.int_en = 0, the reset value 4.7.3, p. 27 8 VSS ground Ground - - 6.1, p. 46 9 VSS ground Ground - - 6.1, p. 46 10 VDD power (VDD) Analog supply, 1.71 V to 3.6 V; any order with VDDIO - - 2, p. 10 Source of this table and of the chip figures: docs/hardware.yml . Never hold SDI, SDO, SCK or CSB high while VDDIO is off: the current through the protection diodes can damage the part (section 4.2). Blocks ¶ Inside the BMP581 Figure description and sources The BMP581's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp ; inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp . The chip compensates both values itself (section 4.1): the data registers and the FIFO hold pressure in pascals and temperature in degrees Celsius as fixed-point numbers, and the driver only converts their scale. Interface selection ¶ After a power-on or soft reset the interface is in I2C mode (section 5.1). With CSB tied to VDDIO it stays there. The first CSB low phase with at least 16 SCK edges changes it to SPI until the next reset; that first frame carries no valid data. The SPI port of the driver sends this dummy read itself, in EnsureInitialized() and again after its soft reset, because a soft reset returns the interface to I2C (table 16). An I2C board must never pull CSB low: the chip would leave I2C mode until the next power cycle. I2C ¶ Address 0x46 with SDO at VSS, 0x47 with SDO at VDDIO (section 5.6); SDO must not float. 100 kHz to 1 MHz (table 4): fast mode plus needs a bus capacitance under 100 pF. A register read is a write of the address, then a read; the chip keeps the address across a STOP, so a repeated START or a STOP and START both work (figures 15, 16). The driver calls WriteRead() . The soft reset (CMD = 0xB6) is not acknowledged (section 7.36); the driver expects the NACK and proves the reset by the reads that follow. BMP581: I2C connection Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp ; inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp . I2C connection (figure chip-circuit-i2c ) Part Kind Value Connects Datasheet U2 MCU - VDD: +VDDIO, GND: GND, SCL: SCL, SDA: SDA, INT: INT 6.2.3, p. 48 R1 resistor 4.7 kΩ (not confirmed: figure 26 shows no pull-up; 4.7 kΩ to VDDIO suits 100 kHz and 400 kHz) +VDDIO, SCL 6.2.3, p. 48 R2 resistor 4.7 kΩ (not confirmed: figure 26 shows no pull-up; 4.7 kΩ to VDDIO suits 100 kHz and 400 kHz) +VDDIO, SDA 6.2.3, p. 48 C1 capacitor 100 nF +VDDIO, GND 6.2.3, p. 48 C2 capacitor 100 nF +VDD, GND 6.2.3, p. 48 SPI 4-wire connection (figure chip-circuit-spi4 ) Part Kind Value Connects Datasheet U2 MCU - VDD: +VDDIO, GND: GND, SCK: SCK, MOSI: MOSI, MISO: MISO, CS: CSB, INT: INT 6.2.2, p. 47 R1 resistor 47 kΩ (not confirmed: figure 25 shows no pull-up; recommended so the SPI selection frame (section 5.1) reads 0xFF) +VDDIO, MISO 6.2.2, p. 47 C1 capacitor 100 nF +VDDIO, GND 6.2.2, p. 47 C2 capacitor 100 nF +VDD, GND 6.2.2, p. 47 Export a circuit for a schematic or PCB tool: kokeb-docs hardware --kicad-netlist OUT.net --circuit i2c . SPI ¶ Four-wire, mode 0 or 3, the mode chosen by SCK at the CSB falling edge (section 5.5); up to 12 MHz with VDDIO at or above 1.62 V, 7 MHz below (table 4). Bit 7 of the first byte is the read flag, bits 6 to 0 the address; read data starts at the second byte, with no dummy byte (figures 8 to 11). CSB stays high at least 80 ns between frames (table 18). After a write to INT_CONFIG the driver waits 1 µs before it reads it back (section 5.5.4); it never uses hybrid bursts. Three-wire SPI (DRIVE_CONFIG.spi3_en) is not supported: the driver never writes DRIVE_CONFIG. A pull-up on MISO (R1, 47 kΩ, not in figure 25) is recommended. After a reset the chip is back in I2C mode, where SDO is an input, and the first frame only selects SPI (section 5.1): MISO floats. With the pull-up the frame reads 0xFF, which every check refuses; without it the driver still runs the reset check after each status read on SPI (see Contract ). The circuit labels SCK and SDI with both hooks, WriteRead() or Transfer() : the diagram tool takes one hook per chip pin for every circuit, and these pins serve both buses. On this circuit they are Transfer() ; on the I2C circuit, WriteRead() (and Write() for the writes). BMP581: SPI 4-wire connection Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp ; inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp . docs.text: After a power-on or soft reset the interface is in I2C mode (section 5.1). With CSB tied to VDDIO it stays there. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( bmp581_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bmp581.git external/driver-bmp581 git submodule update --init external/driver-bmp581 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-bmp581 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE bmp581::bmp581 ) bmp581::bmp581 is an alias of the bmp581 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect BMP581_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver BMP581_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-bmp581 -B build-bmp581 cmake --install build-bmp581 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( bmp581 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE bmp581::bmp581 ) The target is bmp581::bmp581 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated bmp581_version.h go to include/bmp581/inc/ , the template implementation to include/bmp581/src/bmp581.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-bmp581) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-bmp581 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bmp581.git components/bmp581 bmp581 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml bmp581 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : bmp581 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bmp581.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES bmp581 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/bmp581_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into bmp581_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = bmp581 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port, for I2C or for SPI. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Bosch Sensortec BST-BMP581-DS004-13 1.13: Interface selection (I2C, SPI): 5.1 Protocol Selection; Table 16, p. 31 SPI timing: 5.2.1 Interface timing; Table 18 SPI timings, p. 32 SPI protocol: 5.5 SPI Protocol; 5.5.2 SPI Write Operation; 5.5.3 SPI read operation; 5.5.4 SPI hybrid bursts, p. 36 I2C protocol and addresses: 5.6 I2C protocol; 5.6.1 I2C write operation; 5.6.2 I2C read operation, p. 38 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from bmp581::I2cInterface<Self> (in inc/bmp581_i2c_interface.hpp ) or bmp581::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/bmp581_spi_interface.hpp ). The bases use CRTP and declare no hook themselves; the driver template is constrained by the bmp581::BusPort concept, which accepts a class that is exactly one of I2cPort and SpiPort , so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Bosch Sensortec BST-BMP581-DS004-13 1.13: Forced mode: 4.3.3 FORCED mode, p. 16 Pins and connection diagrams: 6.1 Pin Out; 6.2 Connection Diagrams; Table 28, p. 46 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated BMP581, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/bmp581_host_example BMP581 driver 0.1.0 on the host bmp581: initialised 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C bmp581: deinitialised Two forced measurements, then two in normal mode with data ready. The same calls run on your MCU with its port. 1. Wire the chip ¶ The I2C connection of the datasheet (section 6.2.3): CSB to VDDIO selects I2C at power-up, SDO sets the address. BMP581 pin Connect to Notes VDDIO (1) Your MCU's I/O supply 1.08 V to 3.6 V, 100 nF to GND VDD (10) 1.71 V to 3.6 V 100 nF to GND; any order with VDDIO VSS (3, 8, 9) GND SCK (2) I2C SCL Pull-up to VDDIO SDI (4) I2C SDA Pull-up to VDDIO SDO (5) VSS Address 0x46 ( i2c::kI2cAddress ); VDDIO gives 0x47 . Never floating CSB (6) VDDIO Tied high from power-up: I2C mode INT (7) GND, or an MCU input Leave INT_CONFIG.int_en = 0 (the default) when tied to GND For SPI and the full pin table see Hardware . 2. Write the port ¶ The driver calls your class for the bus and the waits. This one forwards to your SDK; platform_* stand for its calls (STM32 HAL, ESP-IDF, Zephyr, Linux i2c-dev): class MyPort : public bmp581 :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, the bytes (register first), STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } // Write the register address, then read with a repeated START in between. bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the chip's reset and conversion times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; The port for SPI and the optional hooks: Porting . 3. Take a measurement ¶ #include "bmp581.hpp" int read_pressure ( MyPort & port , float & pascals , float & celsius ) { bmp581 :: BMP581 < MyPort > sensor ( port , bmp581 :: ForcedPreset ()); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. soft reset, CHIP_ID, NVM ready, Config return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // NoDevice, Bus or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring } const auto m = sensor . MeasureOnce (); // 2. one forced measurement, then standby if ( ! m ) { return static_cast < int > ( m . error ); // every failure is an Error, never a number } pascals = bmp581 :: PressurePa ( m . value . pressure_raw ); // 3. 1/64 Pa, exact celsius = bmp581 :: TemperatureC ( m . value . temperature_raw ); // 1/65536 °C, exact return 0 ; } EnsureInitialized() soft-resets the chip, checks CHIP_ID, NVM readiness and the reset flag, and writes the configuration in standby, reading it back. MeasureOnce() runs one forced measurement and returns the values the chip compensated; nothing that is not a measurement is ever returned as one. Every call returns Result<T> : test it before using the value. When a call fails, Troubleshooting maps each Error to its likely cause. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/bmp581_host_example BMP581 driver 0.1.0 on the host bmp581: initialised 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C 101325.000 Pa 21.5000 C bmp581: deinitialised Two forced measurements, then two in normal mode with data ready. The same calls run on your MCU with its port.

docs.text: The I2C connection of the datasheet (section 6.2.3): CSB to VDDIO selects I2C at power-up, SDO sets the address. BMP581 pin Connect to Notes VDDIO (1) Your MCU's I/O supply 1.08 V to 3.6 V, 100 nF to GND VDD (10) 1.71 V to 3.6 V 100 nF to GND; any order with VDDIO VSS (3, 8, 9) GND SCK (2) I2C SCL Pull-up to VDDIO SDI (4) I2C SDA Pull-up to VDDIO SDO (5) VSS Address 0x46 ( i2c::kI2cAddress ); VDDIO gives 0x47 . Never floating CSB (6) VDDIO Tied high from power-up: I2C mode INT (7) GND, or an MCU input Leave INT_CONFIG.int_en = 0 (the default) when tied to GND For SPI and the full pin table see Hardware .

docs.text: The driver calls your class for the bus and the waits. This one forwards to your SDK; platform_* stand for its calls (STM32 HAL, ESP-IDF, Zephyr, Linux i2c-dev): class MyPort : public bmp581 :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, the bytes (register first), STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } // Write the register address, then read with a repeated START in between. bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the chip's reset and conversion times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; The port for SPI and the optional hooks: Porting .
docs.title: 2. Write the port

docs.text: #include "bmp581.hpp" int read_pressure ( MyPort & port , float & pascals , float & celsius ) { bmp581 :: BMP581 < MyPort > sensor ( port , bmp581 :: ForcedPreset ()); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. soft reset, CHIP_ID, NVM ready, Config return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // NoDevice, Bus or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring } const auto m = sensor . MeasureOnce (); // 2. one forced measurement, then standby if ( ! m ) { return static_cast < int > ( m . error ); // every failure is an Error, never a number } pascals = bmp581 :: PressurePa ( m . value . pressure_raw ); // 3. 1/64 Pa, exact celsius = bmp581 :: TemperatureC ( m . value . temperature_raw ); // 1/65536 °C, exact return 0 ; } EnsureInitialized() soft-resets the chip, checks CHIP_ID, NVM readiness and the reset flag, and writes the configuration in standby, reading it back. MeasureOnce() runs one forced measurement and returns the values the chip compensated; nothing that is not a measurement is ever returned as one. Every call returns Result<T> : test it before using the value. When a call fails, Troubleshooting maps each Error to its likely cause.

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply , and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-<chip> # the plan: every setting that would change python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, security, Actions, rulesets, labels A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md .
