docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a register model of the BMP581, on I2C and on SPI, with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_bmp581.cpp Lifecycle, configuration (every field where section 7 puts it), power modes, forced and normal measurements, exact conversions, the range checks, the FIFO, interrupts, raw access, Deinitialize() , Validate() against table 7 tests/test_reset.cpp A power-on reset found by every call, confirmed by a second read, never written over; a reset at every transfer of ApplyConfig() ; pending checks; standby and Deinitialize() never refused tests/test_bus_faults.cpp Stuck, floating, looped-back and deaf lines at start-up and after; NACKs; lost acknowledgements; dropped and corrupt writes and reads at every transfer; the configuration left in doubt tests/test_timing.cpp The open readings, each under every value: an NVM download that overwrites the marker (no false reset, a real one still found); the second data read of Verify::ReadBack ; odr_is_valid 0, 600 and 3000 us late; a forced mode shown late; deep standby losing writes or not, over every flow; the FIFO flush wait; all 256 fills of the SPI selection frame; a reset during ApplyConfig() with its por read disturbed; standby after a failed first start tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( bmp581_fuzz_bmp581_corpus ), see below tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value (16 and up) is returned by some call tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header (also against a 9.8.7 probe) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , a DelayUs(uint16_t) , a misdeclared GetLastFailure() , an I2C or SPI hook with a narrowed parameter or without noexcept , a port of both buses, an invalid CheckedConfig , a class that is not a port tests/mock_bmp581.hpp The register model, with its own register map and a virtual clock; the I2C and SPI framing and the fault injection are in mock_bmp581_bus.hpp tests/test_model.cpp The model's register map, reset values, timing and tables against the driver's, with static_assert , and the model's own behaviour tests/check_version_copy.cmake _config/Doxyfile carries the CMake version examples/host/ The host example, built with the test flags and run ( bmp581_host_example ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(bmp581) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model stands alone ¶ tests/mock_bmp581.hpp is written from the datasheet, not from the driver: it does not include bmp581_registers.hpp or bmp581_types.hpp . Its register map, field masks, reset values, timing and tables are its own (namespace bmp581_test::chip , each with the datasheet section), so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model (handbook KB-TST-030). tests/test_model.cpp compares the two at compile time: // Register map (section 7). static_assert ( chip :: kChipId == reg :: kChipId && chip :: kRevId == reg :: kRevId && chip :: kChipStatus == reg :: kChipStatus && chip :: kDriveConfig == reg :: kDriveConfig ); static_assert ( chip :: kIntConfig == reg :: kIntConfig && chip :: kIntSource == reg :: kIntSource && chip :: kFifoConfig == reg :: kFifoConfig && chip :: kFifoCount == reg :: kFifoCount && chip :: kFifoSel == reg :: kFifoSel ); static_assert ( chip :: kTempXlsb == reg :: kTempXlsb && chip :: kPressXlsb == reg :: kPressXlsb && chip :: kIntStatus == reg :: kIntStatus && chip :: kStatus == reg :: kStatus && chip :: kFifoData == reg :: kFifoData ); static_assert ( chip :: kNvmAddr == reg :: kNvmAddr && chip :: kNvmDataLsb == reg :: kNvmDataLsb && chip :: kNvmDataMsb == reg :: kNvmDataMsb && chip :: kDspConfig == reg :: kDspConfig && chip :: kDspIir == reg :: kDspIir ); static_assert ( chip :: kOorThrPLsb == reg :: kOorThrPLsb && chip :: kOorThrPMsb == reg :: kOorThrPMsb && chip :: kOorRange == reg :: kOorRange && chip :: kOorConfig == reg :: kOorConfig && chip :: kOsrConfig == reg :: kOsrConfig && chip :: kOdrConfig == reg :: kOdrConfig && chip :: kOsrEff == reg :: kOsrEff && chip :: kCmd == reg :: kCmd ); // Reset values, identity and commands (sections 4.3.9, 7). static_assert ( chip :: kChipIdValue == bmp581 :: kChipId && chip :: kIntConfigReset == reg :: kIntConfigReset && chip :: kDspConfigReset == reg :: kDspConfigReset && chip :: kOdrConfigReset == reg :: kOdrConfigReset && chip :: kSoftResetCommand == reg :: kCmdSoftReset ); static_assert ( chip :: kDataResetByte * 0x01'0101U == reg :: kDataReset && chip :: kFifoEmptyByte == reg :: kFifoEmpty ); // Fields (sections 7.21, 7.22, 7.33, 7.34). static_assert ( chip :: kPor == reg :: kIntPor && chip :: kDrdy == reg :: kIntDrdy && chip :: kFifoFull == reg :: kIntFifoFull && chip :: kFifoThs == reg :: kIntFifoThs && chip :: kOorP == reg :: kIntOorP ); static_assert ( chip :: kNvmRdy == reg :: kStatusNvmRdy && chip :: kNvmErr == reg :: kStatusNvmErr && chip :: kNvmCmdErr == reg :: kStatusNvmCmdErr && chip :: kPressEn == reg :: kOsrPressEn && chip :: kDeepDis == reg :: kOdrDeepDis ); // Timing (table 4). static_assert ( chip :: kSoftResetMaxUs == bmp581 :: kSoftResetUs && chip :: kPowerUpMaxUs == bmp581 :: kPowerUpUs && chip :: kStandbyMaxUs == bmp581 :: kStandbyUs && chip :: kStartupMaxUs == bmp581 :: kStartupUs && chip :: kStartupDeepMaxUs == bmp581 :: kStartupDeepUs ); static_assert ( chip :: kConvPUs == bmp581 :: detail :: kConvPressureUs && chip :: kConvTUs == bmp581 :: detail :: kConvTemperatureUs ); The model changes state on its own ¶ A model that changes only when the driver writes it cannot catch a missed reset. This one, on its virtual clock ( Elapse() , driven by the mock port's DelayUs() and by every frame): resets mid-session ( PowerOnReset() , or before any chosen transfer): every register back to its reset value, INT_STATUS.por set, the FIFO empty, the interface back in I2C mode, no answer for its boot time, then STATUS.status_nvm_rdy; completes measurements in time: forced mode returns to standby after the start-up and the conversion (longer from deep standby), normal mode measures once per data rate period, continuous mode back to back; each updates the data registers, sets drdy, fills the FIFO (streaming or stop-on-full, with decimation) and runs the out-of-range count; completes a commanded standby after a delay, reports the mode it is in, loses writes to the standby-only registers outside standby, and NACKs the soft reset on I2C; reads FIFO_DATA without incrementing the address, keeps a partly read frame, and returns 0x7F when empty; offers both readings where the datasheet is open: the standby read-back at once or after the transition ( standby_delay_us ), INT_STATUS showing disabled sources or not ( flags_for_disabled_sources ), a new mode (forced included) shown late ( mode_lag_us ), OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid shown late on its own ( odr_valid_lag_us ), deep standby losing every write but ODR_CONFIG and CMD or not ( deep_standby_drops_writes , on by default: the strict reading), the NVM download of a measurement from deep standby reaching NVM_DATA or not ( nvm_download_rewrites_data , with the value it leaves, nvm_download_data : the tests use 0x0000, another word and the marker itself), and what MISO shows in the SPI selection frame ( select_fill ); the reset and doubt tests run under both, and tests/test_timing.cpp runs every flow under each. The bus mock adds the faults: an address NACK on any transfer, a data NACK part-way, a lost acknowledgement, a dropped write, a corrupt byte in any read, a line stuck low, floating high, looped back (SPI) or deaf from any transfer on. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_bmp581.cpp lets libFuzzer choose the bus, a configuration, then up to 64 driver calls, and on every bus transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, lose its acknowledgement, flip bits of the data read or drop an acknowledged write, replace the data read by a stuck or floating line, reset the chip just before it, or let 2 ms pass first. The chip may answer at once after a reset or stay silent for its boot time, and on SPI the first frame after a reset only selects SPI again, with the data the fuzzer chooses. Between calls it lets time pass, changes the pressure and temperature (the reset value and out-of-range values included), resets the chip and flips the model's open readings (the standby delay, disabled sources, deep standby losing writes, the NVM download reaching NVM_DATA and the value it leaves, the mode and odr_is_valid lags, the SPI selection fill). After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a call returns an Error the enum defines; a failed value is T{} ; InvalidArgument sent nothing; before the first start nothing but Deinitialize() makes a transfer, and standby once a start has reached the chip; DeviceReset leaves the driver uninitialised; no stuck-line value is ever data: a call whose data read was replaced by all 0x00 or all 0xFF never returns Ok ; every measurement and FIFO sample returned Ok is inside the measurement range and never the reset value, and equals what the chip sent when no read of the call was tampered with; a reset is never missed: after a power-on reset no call that checks for one returns Ok , except a call whose own fault (a flipped or replaced read, the reset itself) it cannot see, and the next call is checked again; nothing is written over a reset chip except in the call during which the reset happened or a read was tampered with, and in EnsureInitialized() , which starts from the soft reset; both reset promises hold on the call after one in which the chip reset and a read was disturbed: the marker in NVM_DATA, which no call but the start writes, shows the reset that the call's own writes hid from the sentinel (see Contract ); every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang. On macOS, Homebrew's LLVM: link its libc++, and add -Wl,-ld_classic. cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DBMP581_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_bmp581 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_bmp581 -max_total_time = 300 -max_len = 512 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bmp581 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_bmp581 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bmp581/ on GCC and Clang ( bmp581_fuzz_bmp581_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise, so a fixed bug stays fixed: check-overwrote-data (the reset check read into the buffer a measurement was still decoded from), invalid-argument-after-check (an argument refused after a pending check had sent a read), reset-hidden-by-failed-sequence (a reset and a corrupt INT_STATUS read inside a failing configuration sequence, now a restart), reset-and-disturbed-read-in-one-call (a reset covered by the sequence's own writes, now found by the marker), sentinel-rewritten-then-setter (after such a call the next setter wrote before it read the por; setters now read INT_STATUS first, and the whole configuration decides a por the sentinel contradicts) and por-on-soft-reset (a power-on reset on the soft reset write itself, a fault of the model's bookkeeping, not of the driver) and standby-after-failed-start (standby sent after a failed first start that reached the chip, as it must be) and stuck-second-data-read (the second data read of Verify::ReadBack stuck low, outvoted by the third: a correct value, which the invariant first took for stuck-line data). CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( bmp581_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/bmp581.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target bmp581_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ Nothing here has run on a BMP581 yet: every behaviour is not verified on hardware . The bench steps, on the ESP32 example ( Examples ) or any port, each with what passes: EnsureInitialized() on I2C at 0x46 and 0x47 , and on SPI: Ok , GetRevision() 0x32. Log the reads of the start-up: INT_STATUS 0x10 then 0x00; STATUS with status_nvm_rdy set on the first poll or within a few. Read 0x23 to 0x26 with ReadRegister() in each power mode: 0x00 every time (the driver refuses a data frame otherwise). Write DSP_IIR with a pressure coefficient through ApplyConfig() : it reads back with set_iir_p in bits 5..3, as the register map says (the field description gives offset 0 for both). MeasureOnce() at x1/x1 and at x128/x128, from deep standby and from standby: Ok , and the time between the forced write and pwr_mode reading 0 within ForcedMeasurementMaxUs() . Breathe on the chip: the temperature rises; lift it 1 m: the pressure falls by about 12 Pa. Normal mode at a table 7 limit (x8/x1 at 140 Hz): ConfigRejected never, OSR_EFF bit 7 set; one step above the table (rejected by Validate() ) written by hand: OSR_EFF bit 7 clear. Note when the bit is updated (at the ODR or OSR write, or at the mode change). A brown-out: pull VDD below 1 V for 10 ms while streaming. The next ReadMeasurement() or WaitDataReady() returns DeviceReset , and EnsureInitialized() starts the chip again. On SPI, the first frame after the reset reads garbage and the call still ends in DeviceReset . FIFO: FifoPreset() for 2 s, then ReadFifo() : 16 frames, each Ok ; a FIFO left until it overflows in stop-on-full mode keeps the oldest frames. SPI at 10 MHz with the CSB setup time of your MCU: no InvalidReply over 10 000 reads. Deep standby and writes (section 4.3): after a soft reset, write OOR_RANGE through the port (outside the driver) and read it back with ReadRegister(0x34) , once straight away and once after ODR_CONFIG = standby with deep_dis = 1 and 2.5 ms. Record whether the first write lands; the driver assumes it may not and always takes the second path. odr_is_valid timing: log OSR_EFF on every poll after SetPowerMode(PowerMode::Normal) at a valid setting. Record the poll on which bit 7 first reads 1; it must be within 4 ms (the driver's deadline). Forced mode timing: log ODR_CONFIG on every poll after the forced write. Record the first poll that shows pwr_mode = forced; it must be within t_startup (3 ms). The NVM_DATA marker: start the driver, then run MeasureOnce() from deep standby 1000 times and leave normal mode with deep standby ( LowPowerPreset() ) for 10 minutes. Record what ReadRegister(0x2C) and 0x2D read (0x3C and 0xC3, or an NVM word, 0x0000 included: the NVM is downloaded at the start of each measurement from deep standby, section 7.22). Either way ApplyConfig() never returns DeviceReset (the marker is verified or written before each sequence), and a brown-out clears both to 0x00 and gives DeviceReset . SPI selection frame: with and without the MISO pull-up, log the bytes of the first frame after a brown-out: 0xFF with the pull-up; whatever they are, the next call returns DeviceReset . FIFO flush: with FifoPreset() , read FIFO_COUNT right after SetPowerMode(PowerMode::Continuous) returns (it waits t_reconf): 0 or a count that grows from there, never a stale count. The soft reset from deep standby: with the default Config (deep standby), send CMD = 0xB6 through the port without the ODR_CONFIG write before it, and read INT_STATUS: record whether por is set. The driver writes ODR_CONFIG = standby with deep_dis = 1 first either way. ReadMeasurement(Verify::ReadBack) 100 000 times in continuous mode at the fastest rate: never InvalidReply on a clean bus. Record the board, the bus, the steps run and their result in the pull request's bench-status section.

docs.text: The tests build the real driver against a register model of the BMP581, on I2C and on SPI, with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_bmp581.cpp Lifecycle, configuration (every field where section 7 puts it), power modes, forced and normal measurements, exact conversions, the range checks, the FIFO, interrupts, raw access, Deinitialize() , Validate() against table 7 tests/test_reset.cpp A power-on reset found by every call, confirmed by a second read, never written over; a reset at every transfer of ApplyConfig() ; pending checks; standby and Deinitialize() never refused tests/test_bus_faults.cpp Stuck, floating, looped-back and deaf lines at start-up and after; NACKs; lost acknowledgements; dropped and corrupt writes and reads at every transfer; the configuration left in doubt tests/test_timing.cpp The open readings, each under every value: an NVM download that overwrites the marker (no false reset, a real one still found); the second data read of Verify::ReadBack ; odr_is_valid 0, 600 and 3000 us late; a forced mode shown late; deep standby losing writes or not, over every flow; the FIFO flush wait; all 256 fills of the SPI selection frame; every chip-specific value (16 and up) is returned by some call tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header (also against a 9.8.7 probe) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , a DelayUs(uint16_t) , a misdeclared GetLastFailure() , an I2C or SPI hook with a narrowed parameter or without noexcept , a port of both buses, an invalid CheckedConfig , a class that is not a port tests/mock_bmp581.hpp The register model, with its own register map and a virtual clock; docs.text: tests/mock_bmp581.hpp is written from the datasheet, not from the driver: it does not include bmp581_registers.hpp or bmp581_types.hpp . static_assert ( chip :: kIntConfig == reg :: kIntConfig && chip :: kIntSource == reg :: kIntSource && chip :: kFifoConfig == reg :: kFifoConfig && chip :: kFifoCount == reg :: kFifoCount && chip :: kFifoSel == reg :: kFifoSel ); static_assert ( chip :: kTempXlsb == reg :: kTempXlsb && chip :: kPressXlsb == reg :: kPressXlsb && chip :: kIntStatus == reg :: kIntStatus && chip :: kStatus == reg :: kStatus && chip :: kFifoData == reg :: kFifoData ); static_assert ( chip :: kNvmAddr == reg :: kNvmAddr && chip :: kNvmDataLsb == reg :: kNvmDataLsb && chip :: kNvmDataMsb == reg :: kNvmDataMsb && chip :: kDspConfig == reg :: kDspConfig && chip :: kDspIir == reg :: kDspIir ); docs.text: A model that changes only when the driver writes it cannot catch a missed reset. This one, on its virtual clock ( Elapse() , driven by the mock port's DelayUs() and by every frame): resets mid-session ( PowerOnReset() , or before any chosen transfer): every register back to its reset value, INT_STATUS.por set, the FIFO empty, the interface back in I2C mode, no answer for its boot time, then STATUS.status_nvm_rdy; completes measurements in time: forced mode returns to standby after the start-up and the conversion (longer from deep standby), normal mode measures once per data rate period, continuous mode back to back; each updates the data registers, sets drdy, fills the FIFO (streaming or stop-on-full, with decimation) and runs the out-of-range count; completes a commanded standby after a delay, reports the mode it is in, loses writes to the standby-only registers outside standby, and NACKs the soft reset on I2C; reads FIFO_DATA without incrementing the address, keeps a partly read frame, and returns 0x7F when empty; offers both readings where the datasheet is open: the standby read-back at once or after the transition ( standby_delay_us ), INT_STATUS showing disabled sources or not ( flags_for_disabled_sources ), a new mode (forced included) shown late ( mode_lag_us ), OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid shown late on its own ( odr_valid_lag_us ), deep standby losing every write but ODR_CONFIG and CMD or not ( deep_standby_drops_writes , on by default: the strict reading), the NVM download of a measurement from deep standby reaching NVM_DATA or not ( nvm_download_rewrites_data , with the value it leaves, nvm_download_data : the tests use 0x0000, another word and the marker itself), and what MISO shows in the SPI selection frame ( select_fill ); the reset and doubt tests run under both, and tests/test_timing.cpp runs every flow under each. The bus mock adds the faults: an address NACK on any transfer, a data NACK part-way, a lost acknowledgement, a dropped write, a corrupt byte in any read, a line stuck low, floating high, looped back (SPI) or deaf from any transfer on.

docs.text: Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_bmp581.cpp lets libFuzzer choose the bus, a configuration, then up to 64 driver calls, and on every bus transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, lose its acknowledgement, flip bits of the data read or drop an acknowledged write, replace the data read by a stuck or floating line, reset the chip just before it, or let 2 ms pass first. The chip may answer at once after a reset or stay silent for its boot time, and on SPI the first frame after a reset only selects SPI again, with the data the fuzzer chooses. Between calls it lets time pass, changes the pressure and temperature (the reset value and out-of-range values included), resets the chip and flips the model's open readings (the standby delay, disabled sources, deep standby losing writes, the NVM download reaching NVM_DATA and the value it leaves, the mode and odr_is_valid lags, the SPI selection fill). After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a call returns an Error the enum defines; a failed value is T{} ; InvalidArgument sent nothing; before the first start nothing but Deinitialize() makes a transfer, and standby once a start has reached the chip; DeviceReset leaves the driver uninitialised; no stuck-line value is ever data: a call whose data read was replaced by all 0x00 or all 0xFF never returns Ok ; every measurement and FIFO sample returned Ok is inside the measurement range and never the reset value, and equals what the chip sent when no read of the call was tampered with; a reset is never missed: after a power-on reset no call that checks for one returns Ok , except a call whose own fault (a flipped or replaced read, the reset itself) it cannot see, and the next call is checked again; nothing is written over a reset chip except in the call during which the reset happened or a read was tampered with, and in EnsureInitialized() , which starts from the soft reset; both reset promises hold on the call after one in which the chip reset and a read was disturbed: the marker in NVM_DATA, which no call but the start writes, shows the reset that the call's own writes hid from the sentinel (see Contract ); every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang. On macOS, Homebrew's LLVM: link its libc++, and add -Wl,-ld_classic. cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DBMP581_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_bmp581 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_bmp581 -max_total_time = 300 -max_len = 512 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bmp581 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_bmp581 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bmp581/ on GCC and Clang ( bmp581_fuzz_bmp581_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise, so a fixed bug stays fixed: check-overwrote-data (the reset check read into the buffer a measurement was still decoded from), invalid-argument-after-check (an argument refused after a pending check had sent a read), reset-hidden-by-failed-sequence (a reset and a corrupt INT_STATUS read inside a failing configuration sequence, now a restart), reset-and-disturbed-read-in-one-call (a reset covered by the sequence's own writes, now found by the marker), sentinel-rewritten-then-setter (after such a call the next setter wrote before it read the por; setters now read INT_STATUS first, and the whole configuration decides a por the sentinel contradicts) and por-on-soft-reset (a power-on reset on the soft reset write itself, a fault of the model's bookkeeping, not of the driver) and standby-after-failed-start (standby sent after a failed first start that reached the chip, as it must be) and stuck-second-data-read (the second data read of Verify::ReadBack stuck low, outvoted by the third: a correct value, which the invariant first took for stuck-line data). CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ).

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBMP581_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( bmp581_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/bmp581.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.

The bench steps, on the ESP32 example ( Examples ) or any port, each with what passes: EnsureInitialized() on I2C at 0x46 and 0x47 , and on SPI: Ok , GetRevision() 0x32. Log the reads of the start-up: INT_STATUS 0x10 then 0x00; STATUS with status_nvm_rdy set on the first poll or within a few. Read 0x23 to 0x26 with ReadRegister() in each power mode: 0x00 every time (the driver refuses a data frame otherwise). Write DSP_IIR with a pressure coefficient through ApplyConfig() : it reads back with set_iir_p in bits 5..3, as the register map says (the field description gives offset 0 for both). MeasureOnce() at x1/x1 and at x128/x128, from deep standby and from standby: Ok , and the time between the forced write and pwr_mode reading 0 within ForcedMeasurementMaxUs() . Breathe on the chip: the temperature rises; lift it 1 m: the pressure falls by about 12 Pa. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Bosch Sensortec BST-BMP581-DS004-13 1.13: Normal mode and the ODR/OSR check: 4.3.4 NORMAL mode; Table 7 maximum nominal ODR setting per OSR settings, p. 17 Post-power-up checks: 4.3.9 Post-power-up procedure, p. 18 I2C protocol and addresses: 5.6 I2C protocol; 5.6.1 I2C write operation; 5.6.2 I2C read operation, p. 38 Identification and status: 7.1 Register (0x01) ASIC identification ID; 7.22 Register (0x28) Status register, p. 51 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice or Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: its EnsureInitialized() returned false , or a transfer did. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). I2C: check the address against SDO ( 0x46 with SDO at VSS, 0x47 at VDDIO), the pull-ups, VDD and VDDIO, and that CSB is tied to VDDIO. One NACK during the start-up is expected: the soft reset write (section 7.36). SPI: check the CSB pin and that the port drives it high between frames. With a logic analyser, check that the first frame (SPI: a CHIP_ID read; I2C: CMD = 0xB6) appears on the bus. EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ CHIP_ID did not read 0x50, or INT_STATUS did not read 0x10 after the soft reset and 0x00 after that. Symptom ( ReadRegister() or a logic analyser) Likely cause Fix CHIP_ID 0x00 SDA or MISO stuck low; on SPI no MISO wire, or a chip still in I2C mode Check continuity; check that CSB toggles CHIP_ID 0xFF The data line floating high, or the chip unpowered Check VDD, VDDIO and SDO CHIP_ID 0x51 or another value Another part (a BMP585 reads 0x51) Check the part marking: "C" is a BMP581 (table 29) CHIP_ID 0x50 , INT_STATUS not 0x10 The soft reset did not reach the chip SPI: check the first frames; I2C: check that the port sends a write even when a NACK follows EnsureInitialized returns Timeout or DeviceFault ¶ Timeout : STATUS.status_nvm_rdy never read 1 within Config::startup_timeout_ms after the soft reset; check the supplies and their ramp (section 4.2). DeviceFault : STATUS reports an NVM error, so the trimming data did not load; a power cycle may clear it, a repeated one means a damaged part. EnsureInitialized or ApplyConfig returns WriteMismatch ¶ A configuration register read back differently from what was written. A single one points at noise on the bus: retry. Every time, on the same register, points at a port that corrupts writes, or at a chip outside standby (the driver always writes in standby, section 4.3.8). SetPowerMode or EnsureInitialized returns ConfigRejected ¶ Normal mode with a data rate the chip does not accept for the oversampling (table 7): OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid still read 0 at the deadline (t_startup_deep, 4 ms, polled every 0.5 ms), and the chip would measure with its own defaults. Validate() refuses the combinations table 7 rules out, so this means the chip disagrees with the table: lower the data rate or the oversampling, and read GetLastOsrEff() for what the chip chose. Reads return InvalidReply ¶ The reply cannot come from the chip: the reserved registers 0x23 to 0x26 did not read 0x00, a reserved bit was set, or the frame was all 0x00. Once now and then: noise; the next call reads again. Every time: a stuck or floating line (pull-ups, SDO, the MISO wire). On SPI the first frame after a power-on reset only selects SPI again and reads as garbage; the driver then checks for the reset itself and returns DeviceReset . A pull-up on MISO makes that frame read 0xFF ( Hardware ). Reads return DeviceReset ¶ The chip reset since the driver started it, usually a dip of VDD or VDDIO, confirmed by OSR_CONFIG reading 0x00 twice. The driver is uninitialised: call EnsureInitialized() . If it repeats, check the supplies, their decoupling (100 nF at each pin) and the inrush current (section 6.2.5). A line stuck low reads the same way; EnsureInitialized() then fails with DeviceIdMismatch . Reads return NoData ¶ The data registers hold their reset value 0x7F7F7F: no measurement since the last reset. Start one: MeasureOnce() , or normal or continuous mode. The driver also checks for a reset first. Reads return OutOfRange ¶ The value lies outside 30 kPa to 125 kPa or -40 °C to 85 °C (tables 1 and 2). In a pressure chamber or a freezer that is the truth; otherwise compare with a reference before trusting the chip. MeasureOnce returns Busy or Timeout ¶ Busy : the configured mode is normal or continuous, or the previous forced measurement still runs; call SetPowerMode(PowerMode::Standby) first. Timeout : the chip did not return to standby within ForcedMeasurementMaxUs() (106 ms at x128 and x128). Check that your port's DelayUs() really waits: a delay that returns at once makes every wait far too short. WaitDataReady returns Unsupported or Timeout ¶ Unsupported : Config::source_data_ready is off (the chip reports drdy only for an enabled source), or the mode is standby. Timeout : no measurement within data_ready_timeout_ms ; it must cover one data rate period (8 s at 0.125 Hz). The pressure jumps when the air moves ¶ That is the air: doors, wind and fans move the pressure by more than the sensor's noise (section 4.4.2). Enable the IIR filter ( pressure_iir , iir_to_data_registers ) and choose the coefficient from table 10.

I2C: check the address against SDO ( 0x46 with SDO at VSS, 0x47 at VDDIO), the pull-ups, VDD and VDDIO, and that CSB is tied to VDDIO. With a logic analyser, check that the first frame (SPI: a CHIP_ID read; I2C: CMD = 0xB6) appears on the bus.
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice or Bus

docs.text: CHIP_ID did not read 0x50, or INT_STATUS did not read 0x10 after the soft reset and 0x00 after that. Symptom ( ReadRegister() or a logic analyser) Likely cause Fix CHIP_ID 0x00 SDA or MISO stuck low; on SPI no MISO wire, or a chip still in I2C mode Check continuity; check that CSB toggles CHIP_ID 0xFF The data line floating high, or the chip unpowered Check VDD, VDDIO and SDO CHIP_ID 0x51 or another value Another part (a BMP585 reads 0x51) Check the part marking: "C" is a BMP581 (table 29) CHIP_ID 0x50 , INT_STATUS not 0x10 The soft reset did not reach the chip SPI: check the first frames; I2C: check that the port sends a write even when a NACK follows
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch

docs.text: Timeout : STATUS.status_nvm_rdy never read 1 within Config::startup_timeout_ms after the soft reset; check the supplies and their ramp (section 4.2). DeviceFault : STATUS reports an NVM error, so the trimming data did not load; a power cycle may clear it, a repeated one means a damaged part.
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns Timeout or DeviceFault

docs.text: A configuration register read back differently from what was written. A single one points at noise on the bus: retry. Every time, on the same register, points at a port that corrupts writes, or at a chip outside standby (the driver always writes in standby, section 4.3.8).
docs.title: EnsureInitialized or ApplyConfig returns WriteMismatch

docs.text: Normal mode with a data rate the chip does not accept for the oversampling (table 7): OSR_EFF.odr_is_valid still read 0 at the deadline (t_startup_deep, 4 ms, polled every 0.5 ms), and the chip would measure with its own defaults. Validate() refuses the combinations table 7 rules out, so this means the chip disagrees with the table: lower the data rate or the oversampling, and read GetLastOsrEff() for what the chip chose.
docs.title: SetPowerMode or EnsureInitialized returns ConfigRejected

docs.text: The reply cannot come from the chip: the reserved registers 0x23 to 0x26 did not read 0x00, a reserved bit was set, or the frame was all 0x00. Once now and then: noise; the next call reads again. Every time: a stuck or floating line (pull-ups, SDO, the MISO wire). On SPI the first frame after a power-on reset only selects SPI again and reads as garbage; the driver then checks for the reset itself and returns DeviceReset . A pull-up on MISO makes that frame read 0xFF ( Hardware ).
docs.title: Reads return InvalidReply

docs.text: The chip reset since the driver started it, usually a dip of VDD or VDDIO, confirmed by OSR_CONFIG reading 0x00 twice. The driver is uninitialised: call EnsureInitialized() . If it repeats, check the supplies, their decoupling (100 nF at each pin) and the inrush current (section 6.2.5). A line stuck low reads the same way; EnsureInitialized() then fails with DeviceIdMismatch .
docs.title: Reads return DeviceReset

docs.text: The data registers hold their reset value 0x7F7F7F: no measurement since the last reset. Start one: MeasureOnce() , or normal or continuous mode. The driver also checks for a reset first.
docs.title: Reads return NoData

docs.text: The value lies outside 30 kPa to 125 kPa or -40 °C to 85 °C (tables 1 and 2). In a pressure chamber or a freezer that is the truth; otherwise compare with a reference before trusting the chip.
docs.title: Reads return OutOfRange

docs.text: Busy : the configured mode is normal or continuous, or the previous forced measurement still runs; call SetPowerMode(PowerMode::Standby) first. Timeout : the chip did not return to standby within ForcedMeasurementMaxUs() (106 ms at x128 and x128). Check that your port's DelayUs() really waits: a delay that returns at once makes every wait far too short.
docs.title: MeasureOnce returns Busy or Timeout

docs.text: Unsupported : Config::source_data_ready is off (the chip reports drdy only for an enabled source), or the mode is standby. Timeout : no measurement within data_ready_timeout_ms ; it must cover one data rate period (8 s at 0.125 Hz).
docs.title: WaitDataReady returns Unsupported or Timeout

docs.text: That is the air: doors, wind and fans move the pressure by more than the sensor's noise (section 4.4.2). Enable the IIR filter ( pressure_iir , iir_to_data_registers ) and choose the coefficient from table 10.
docs.title: The pressure jumps when the air moves
